cohort: The study included 214 inborn very low birth weight infants (VLBWIs) admitted to a NICU between April 2009 and March 2022.
finding: 16.8% of VLBWIs had symptomatic airway diseases, with tracheobronchomalacia (TBM) and pharyngomalacia being common, and these infants tended to have shorter gestational age, lower birth weight, were more often boys, had more moderate/severe BPD, and required stronger respiratory management.
gest_age: N/A (shorter gestational age identified as a risk factor for airway diseases)
